**Nothing blocks this change, but it changes behaviour, so a person at Theorem must decide before it merges.** The Tests run for head `e25ca0f` had not finished when this review read the checks.

**For a person at Theorem to decide**

- Findings of one project that agree on harness, upstream commit, kind, file and function get the same key. The second finding becomes a comment on the first issue, not an issue of its own.
- A new wording under the key of a closed issue goes on that issue as a `held finding update:` comment (`.github/scripts/review-held:267-273`). The summary counts it as "a text added", not as "closed" (`review-held:289-293`).
- The layout of the issue body changes. Line 6 is now `held finding text:`, and the finding starts on line 7, or on line 8 for an issue that holds several. The disclosure route and `an internal tool` read these bodies. Both are outside this repository, so this review did not check them.
- For an issue filed under the old key, the identity uses the model's `project:` line in the issue body (`review-held:177`). It does not use the project the workflow wrote.

<details><summary>Notes that do not block</summary>

- `review-held:50` and the description say the raw key is `<the object's own sha256>`. Line 307 keeps only its first 12 digits.
- `lookup` (`review-held:199`) treats field 5 as a `held finding set:` line without checking that prefix. Match only when `index($5, "held finding set: ") == 1`.
- `lookup` picks a set issue that is listed before a closed issue with the key itself. The comment at `review-held:193-194` describes the opposite order.
- When `why held:` has no colon, `kind` (`review-held:131`) keeps up to 40 characters of prose. In that case harness, repository and commit fall back to `none`, but kind does not.
- The commit is hashed as written (`review-held:128`, `144`), so a short sha and the full sha give two different identities.
- An issue title is cut at 200 characters (`review-held:255`). An issue of the old key is matched through that cut title (`review-held:179`), so a longer title can yield another function, and so another identity.
- Not checked: the identities the description gives for #397, #398, #421, #450, #451 and #372. Those issues are in a private repository.
</details>
